title: ZRAM 与 swap 路径：压缩、换入换出、mm_stat 与延迟代价
key_conclusions: ZRAM delays kills by compressing anonymous pages, but hot swap-in can convert memory pressure into user-visible stalls.
pswpin aligned with PSI is a stronger jank signal than pswpout alone.
mm_stat must be interpreted with vmstat, meminfo, PSI, and victim worksheet fields.
Kill benefit depends on RSS, PSS, swap state, memcg, and whether the victim owns the active anonymous working set.
shallow_points: The article does not validate mm_stat column order on real vendor kernels.
It does not include measured compression ratios from low-end Android devices.
It does not include Perfetto traces showing swap-in latency on UI or RenderThread.
It does not quantify when ZRAM pool pressure should trigger tuning or kill policy changes.
